documents.title: The Jackal and the Sun Child
How the Sun and the Moon Were Made

stories.title: The Lion and the Rabbit
stories.setting: A forest and a deep well.
stories.theme: Intelligence can overcome brute force.
mainEvents: The animals arrange to send the lion one animal per day.
The rabbit arrives late and invents a rival lion.
The rabbit leads the lion to a well, where the lion mistakes his reflection for the rival.
The lion jumps into the well, freeing the other animals.

stories.title: The Laboratory
stories.setting: Mia's house and her father's locked laboratory at night.
stories.theme: Fear can come from mistaken assumptions.
mainEvents: Mia hears a frightening laugh behind the locked laboratory door.
Liz persuades Mia to enter when the door is left unlocked.
The girls panic in the dark room.
Mia's father reveals that the laugh comes from a birthday doll.

stories.title: The Report
stories.setting: A library, an alien ship, outer space, and Earth.
stories.theme: Responsibility and unexpected help can solve a difficult problem.
mainEvents: Lee worries because his part of the group project is unfinished.
An alien takes him into space after hearing his wish for help.
Lee observes the moon and Mars.
The alien helps Lee build a model of Mars and returns him to Earth.

stories.title: The Dog’s Bell
stories.setting: A village and its streets.
stories.theme: A reputation is not admirable when it comes from harmful behavior.
mainEvents: John's dog repeatedly bites villagers.
A friend suggests a bell so people can hear the dog coming.
The dog believes the attention makes him popular.
Other dogs explain that the bell merely helps people avoid him.

stories.title: The Jackal and the Sun Child
stories.setting: A desert, a rock, and a field of flowers.
stories.theme: A tempting reward can hide serious consequences.
mainEvents: The sun child offers the jackal a necklace for carrying her home.
Her heat painfully burns the jackal's back.
The jackal runs and jumps into flowers to make her fall off.
The heat leaves the black mark associated with jackals.

stories.title: The Friendly Ghost
stories.setting: A riverside community during a dark rainstorm.
stories.theme: A frightening appearance can conceal a protective intention.
mainEvents: A kind woman becomes a ghost who still wants to protect children.
Children become lost beside a rising river during a storm.
The ghost frightens and follows them away from the river.
The children reach home before the flood becomes dangerous.

stories.title: The Best Prince
stories.setting: King Minos's palace and kingdom.
stories.theme: Kindness and peace are stronger qualifications for leadership than force.
mainEvents: The sick king must choose one of his three sons as successor.
Theseus and Pelias argue and draw their swords.
Minos chooses peaceful, kind Jason.
The older brothers regret missing their father's final moments and accept Jason.

stories.title: How the Sun and the Moon Were Made
stories.setting: An Inuit party, the woods, and the sky.
stories.theme: Wrongdoing is exposed and carries lasting consequences.
mainEvents: The siblings attend a party.
Someone attacks the girl in darkness.
She uses black dirt in her decorated hair to identify the attacker as her brother.
They chase each other with fire, grow enormous, and become the moon and sun.

stories.title: The Starfish
stories.setting: An island beach at evening after the tide leaves starfish on the sand.
stories.theme: A small action matters to the individual it helps.
mainEvents: The narrator sees many starfish stranded by the waves.
A little girl asks for help and then begins throwing starfish back.
The narrator argues that she cannot save all of them.
She answers that saving one still matters to that starfish.

stories.title: The First Peacock
stories.setting: Ancient Greece and the night sky.
stories.theme: Deception can cause an innocent servant to suffer consequences.
mainEvents: Argos uses his hundred eyes to guard Hera's special cow.
Zeus sends a musician whose song puts Argos to sleep.
Zeus steals the cow and Hera transforms Argos into a peacock.
Argos's eyes appear on the peacock's tail, and Zeus later places his image among the stars.

stories.title: Princess Rose and the Creature
stories.setting: A kingdom, a forest, and the route to Henry's ship.
stories.theme: Acceptance looks beyond outward appearance.
mainEvents: The jealous queen puts Rose to sleep and abandons her in a forest.
Rose dreams of the man she will marry.
She meets the green, horned creature Henry and spends a pleasant day with him.
Rose kisses Henry, who changes into the man from her dream, and they marry.

stories.title: The Crazy Artist
stories.setting: Frenhofer's apartment and the wider art world.
stories.theme: New art may need time before people understand it.
mainEvents: Successful painter Frenhofer abandons his old career to pursue a new method.
He works on one painting for years and neglects his health.
Other artists reject the crowded lines, colors, shapes, and symbols.
Over time, critics and the public recognize the painting's importance.

stories.title: The Farmer and the Cats
stories.setting: A poor farm after a fire, during the autumn harvest.
stories.theme: Unexpected helpers deserve gratitude and care.
mainEvents: A fire leaves poor Arthur and Maria with only their cats and a debt.
The lord threatens punishment if they do not pay after harvest.
Each night, unseen helpers complete as much fieldwork as the farmers.
The cats finish the harvest and leave money; Arthur and Maria discover and reward them.

stories.title: A Magical Book
stories.setting: Sarah's home, school, a local store, and a street.
stories.theme: Power should be used responsibly to help rather than harm.
mainEvents: Sarah receives a gold-paged magical book.
The book gives her power to control people, which she uses for jokes and trouble.
She sees her coach about to walk in front of a bus and stops him with the power.
Sarah limits herself to using the power for good.

stories.title: The Big Race
stories.setting: A long animal race across fields and roads.
stories.theme: Steady effort can defeat careless overconfidence.
mainEvents: A duck sells tickets to a long race between a rabbit and a turtle.
The rabbit quickly gains a large lead.
Certain of victory, the rabbit eats and sleeps.
The turtle keeps moving and reaches the finish first.

stories.title: Adams County’s Gold
stories.setting: Adams Academy and a nearby forest in Adams County.
stories.theme: Curiosity and cooperation turn an ordinary day into discovery.
mainEvents: Tom looks for something fun to do on Saturday.
Brad shows him an 1870 book containing clues to hidden gold.
They interpret a flat tree underground as a buried board and dig for it.
They find a gold coin and a map leading to more treasure.

stories.title: The Race for Water
stories.setting: A riverside town and a hill during a drought.
stories.theme: Water must be appreciated, and clever action can repair communal mistakes.
mainEvents: The townspeople waste abundant river water.
The Sky stops the rain and the river dries.
A boy challenges the Sky to fill puddles before he reaches a hilltop.
Rain runs downhill into the river instead, filling it and teaching the town to conserve water.

stories.title: The Little Red Chicken
stories.setting: A small-town store and the place where the chicken makes bread.
stories.theme: People should work for what they want instead of depending on others.
mainEvents: A cat wants bread, but the chicken's store has only wheat.
The cat refuses the chicken's offer to help make bread.
The chicken grinds the wheat and bakes bread alone.
She refuses to give or sell it to the cat and advises him to grow his own wheat.

stories.title: Shipwrecked
stories.setting: A ship at sea and a remote island.
stories.theme: Hardship can transform a person's values and definition of happiness.
mainEvents: Selfish lawyer Simon loses his job and money and plans a new life abroad.
A wave throws him from a ship, and he reaches an island alone.
He builds shelter and tools, lives on fish and rainwater, and grows content.
When rescuers arrive, Simon refuses to leave his simpler life.

stories.title: The seven cities of gold
stories.setting: A westward Spanish expedition and earthen settlements.
stories.theme: Greed and unquestioned rumors distort how people see real communities.
mainEvents: Coronado hears extravagant reports about seven golden cities.
He leads three hundred men west to find them.
They encounter ordinary earthen cities whose residents feed them and deny that gold exists there.
A final glint of sunlight tempts Coronado, but he accepts the truth and returns home.

stories.title: Katy
stories.setting: A hospital before and after Katy's brain operation.
stories.theme: Kindness and courage can inspire an entire community during illness.
mainEvents: A nurse meets eight-year-old Katy, who has a painful problem at the base of her brain.
Katy uses her limited strength to play with, paint for, and gather flowers for other patients.
Doctors successfully operate on her.
After recovering, Katy returns to read and play with hospital patients.

stories.title: A Better Reward
stories.setting: A restaurant delivery area and the neighborhood around a customer's house.
stories.theme: Compassion can be more rewarding than money or punishment.
mainEvents: Jenny reads about an uncaught food thief and a police reward.
Against Jim's advice, she chases the thief after a delivery is stolen.
She discovers a thin mother dog feeding puppies.
The restaurant workers adopt the dogs, and Jenny values her new dog over the cash reward.

stories.title: The camp
stories.setting: A noisy summer camp near an airport and its forest game area.
stories.theme: Trying an unwanted new experience can reveal confidence and friendship.
mainEvents: Stacie resents being sent to a camp with plain food, swimming, noise, and spider webs.
She attends water-safety class and reluctantly joins a water-gun flag game.
Stacie discovers that she enjoys the game and captures the red flag.
Her blue team wins, and she enjoys the remaining week with new friends.

stories.title: A Strong Friendship
stories.setting: A town buried in snow and narrow passages beneath it.
stories.theme: Different strengths become powerful through cooperation and friendship.
mainEvents: Strong, famous Tim and smart, jealous Jack compete for recognition.
A snowstorm traps the town without food.
Jack finds passages; Tim breaks ice blocks until exhausted.
Jack retrieves food and guides Tim home, teaching both men friendship.

stories.title: Joe’s Pond
stories.setting: A school, a public park, and a trash-filled pond.
stories.theme: Persistent community action can repair a damaged environment.
mainEvents: A school video shows factory trash making river communities sick.
Joe recognizes similar pollution in a park pond.
His grandfather encourages him to continue the family's tradition of helping people.
Joe organizes six weeks of cleanup until the pond is free of trash and safe for swimming.

stories.title: Archie and His Donkey
stories.setting: A long road to town and the town entrance.
stories.theme: Trying to please everyone can destroy one's own judgment and goal.
mainEvents: Archie and Tom take a donkey to town to sell it.
A woman says Archie should ride; a farmer later advises that neither should ride and that they should carry it.
They arrive late while carrying the heavy donkey.
Teenagers mock and stone them; the donkey escapes, leaving Archie with nothing.

stories.title: The Spider and the Bird
stories.setting: A forest web and a flight over the surrounding landscape.
stories.theme: A fair bargain and shared experience can turn fear into friendship.
mainEvents: A spider tests trapped insects with puzzles before deciding whether to eat them.
A bird becomes trapped and bargains for a chance to answer.
She answers 'the sky' to a riddle whose answer is Hawaii and must provide valuable food.
The bird carries the spider on a bug-finding tour, and they become friends.

stories.title: The Party
stories.setting: Cody's new house and garage during a snowstorm.
stories.theme: The presence of loved ones matters more than elaborate entertainment.
mainEvents: Cody plans a birthday party with a band at his new home.
Heavy snow forces the stage indoors, then keeps the band and other performers away.
The party is canceled, and Cody misses his old home and grandparents.
His grandparents arrive despite the delay, and their visit makes the birthday special.

stories.title: How the World Got Light
stories.setting: Darkland, the president's house, and the sky.
stories.theme: Clever resistance can free a resource hoarded by an unjust ruler.
mainEvents: The pig president keeps all light and the sun inside a bag.
The animals hold a contest and choose Raven as the smartest.
Raven imitates a crying baby so the president opens his door.
Raven steals the bag, releases the sun into the sky, and gives everyone light.

stories.title: Cats and Secrets
stories.setting: A market area in an old section of England and a judge's court.
stories.theme: Evidence exposes deception, and a revealed secret cannot be hidden again.
mainEvents: A dishonest seller offers Beth a cheap baby pig.
He gives her a closed bag containing a cat instead.
When he returns, Beth and her friends take the case to a judge.
Beth opens the seller's bag, releases another cat as evidence, and exposes his secret.
